text:
jordan: Hey team — had a specialist visit (orthopedics) last week and insurance denied the claim saying 'missing PCP referral/authorization'. EOB attached. Anyone been through this and know the fastest way to get it paid without rebooking?
maya (People Ops): Sorry that happened, ugh. First step is to ask your PCP office for the referral/authorization number they submitted (or request they submit it retroactively). You need that auth number + the date range. Then resubmit the claim as a 'claim correction' or 'claim appeal' via the insurer portal with the EOB and the referral attached. If the PCP refuses, we can escalate.
samir: I dealt with this with Anthem a couple months ago. Quick checklist I used: 1) Call PCP office, ask for the 'authorization number' and the fax/confirmation they sent. 2) Get a scanned PDF of the referral/authorization. 3) Download EOB from member portal. 4) Go to member portal -> Claims -> Dispute/Correct -> Upload docs and include a short cover note. Took ~2 weeks to process.
jordan: Do we have a short cover note template I can paste into the portal? Anthem's free-text field is tiny and I don't want to miss key fields.
maya (People Ops): Yep — here's a minimal template you can paste into the portal message field:

```
Requesting claim correction for claim #<insert claim number>.
Date of service: <mm/dd/yyyy>.
Rendering provider: <Dr. Name> (NPI <number>).
PCP referral/auth number: <AUTH-#####>.
Attached: EOB, referral/authorization from PCP office.
Member contact: <your phone/email>.
```

Include the claim number from your EOB, the exact date of service, and the auth number. If you only have a PCP note, ask the office to generate an authorization letter with the auth number — that's what claims teams look for.

hr-bot: Reminder: To add supporting docs for benefits claims, upload PDFs to the Benefits Portal -> Claims -> "Upload Supporting Documents" within 30 days of EOB to avoid delays.

anthem-support: Hi Jordan — we can reopen the claim as a correction. Please DM us your member ID and the claim number and attach the referral. We'll flag it for manual review once documents are attached.

jordan: Thanks @maya and @samir — I'll call the PCP now. @anthem-support I'll DM the claim number once I have the referral. If anyone from People Ops can confirm the wording of the referral letter is enough after I get it, please ping. :thumbsup:
maya (People Ops): Happy to review the referral letter before you submit. If PCP gives only a fax confirmation, scan it and include a short cover note showing the fax confirmation number and timestamp.
samir: FWIW, also check the provider's billing NPI matches the one on the claim — Anthem sometimes creates a mismatch and routes to pending. Good luck! :+1:
